by.claim: RFC-002 declares "implementing a change promotion system" a Non-Goal and makes push-to-stage depend on "some external system to move changes to the deployment branch," yet that unbuilt dependency is already load-bearing: T-26443 reports that in push-to-stage mode auto-sync deploys whatever the stage branch last held because the external promoter has not yet moved the fresh manifests, and note-1 records that the stage-branch promoter is still a shell script with no owner. The correctness of hydrated deployments rests on a component the design puts out of scope and the org has not staffed.

The PRD's Risks and Mitigations section asserts "No immediate Risks to consider," but the exact semantics it proposes for `Reverse` — waiting for one Application to be fully deleted before moving to the next — is the mechanism T-28511 reports as a defect: an Application stuck in Progressing never completes deletion, the wait never returns, and the controller restarts the deletion wave from the top, producing an infinite delete/re-create loop. The risk is not hypothetical; it is filed against the behavior the PRD is proposing to ship.

The user-facing promise RFC-001 is sold on — decoupling sync from control-plane privileges so administrators can hold least-privilege cluster credentials — is inverted in practice by the diff path: T-28695 reports that sync honors `destinationServiceAccounts` but Server-Side Diff runs as the cluster Secret credential, and because Kubernetes RBAC has no dry-run verb, computing a diff demands real `patch` authority on every resource kind in the Application, expanded five times with no end state. Turning on the feature that is meant to shrink standing privilege forces the standing cluster credential to grow.

The roadmap and the PRD make opposite promises about the same field: strategy.md states that ordered or automated deletion of ApplicationSet children "will not be implemented" and that teardown remains a manual operator action performed one Application at a time, while the PRD specifies a `deletionOrder` field on `ApplicationSetStrategy` with a `Reverse` value that deletes children in reverse RollingSync step order, waiting for each to be fully deleted before the next. Both cannot hold; note-2 records the disagreement being raised at the incident review and explicitly left unowned ("needs an owner. not deciding here"), so no one currently owns the call.

The incident review's interim rule — hydrator pilot repos must not use progressive sync until there is a debounce, because each hydrator push restarts the rolling sync wave — is contradicted by work already in flight and already requested: T-27949 is a pilot repo running the source hydrator and RollingSync together, with each hydration commit picked up as a source change, and T-24578 asks for Source Hydrator support in ApplicationSets specifically to control destroy ordering. The restriction was recorded as something the pilot ticket "should carry"; until it does, the roadmap demand and the operational prohibition point opposite ways.

T-28927 proposes promoting Progressive Sync from beta to Stable on the argoproj definition requiring the feature be "tested and validated with various use cases," but the data to make that judgement does not exist: T-27846 states that getting a wide-eye view of progressive sync is difficult and asks for metrics that would answer how long a step took and which Applications a sync is waiting on, and T-27949 reports its live failure with the note that ApplicationSet controller logs were at warn level so no progressive-sync transition logs were emitted at all. The stability bar is stated without an instrument that can measure it.

The roadmap and the PRD make opposite promises about the same field: strategy.md states that ordered or automated deletion of ApplicationSet children "will not be implemented" and that teardown remains a manual operator action performed one Application at a time, while the PRD specifies a `deletionOrder` field on `ApplicationSetStrategy` with a `Reverse` value that deletes children in reverse RollingSync step order, waiting for each to be fully deleted before the next. Both cannot hold; note-2 records the disagreement being raised at the incident review and explicitly left unowned ("needs an owner. not deciding here"), so no one currently owns the call.

The PRD's Non-Goals rely on a UI surface the roadmap says does not manage this at all: the PRD accepts that a user selecting the unsupported `custom` deletion strategy gets "a configuration field that accepts input but ignores it silently" in the UI, while strategy.md states that first-class UI/CLI/API support for ApplicationSet resources "does not include the ability to manage the deletion order of child applications through these interfaces." Either the UI exposes `deletionOrder` (and the roadmap statement is false) or it does not (and the PRD's silently-ignored-field behavior cannot occur as described).

distractorGate.note: DX1/DX2 violations fail rung 3 for runs scored from this date; score files recorded earlier are never regenerated and keep their as-run results. Evidence: five distractor-disciplined runs (two single-pass, three composed dispatch-shape) all clean; every run before the discipline paragraph violated at least one.
